--- title: "NBA reference" subtitle: "sportsdataverse.nba — hand-written, executable" --- A representative slice of the `sportsdataverse.nba` ESPN surface, documented the same way as [MLB](mlb.qmd): signature + parameters + returns table + an **executable example that renders the real frame**. --- ## `espn_nba_teams` ```python espn_nba_teams(return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame ``` The full NBA team directory from ESPN's Site v2 API. **Parameters** | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame; else polars. | **Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per team (same tidy column set as every other league's `espn__teams`). **Example** ::: {#eec28877 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams teams = espn_nba_teams() print("shape:", teams.shape) teams.select(["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]).head(10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` shape: (30, 14) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: --- ## `espn_nba_team_roster` ```python espn_nba_team_roster(team_id: int | str, *, return_parsed: bool = True, return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame | dict ``` A single team's roster. Parser-backed, so `return_parsed=True` is the default. **Parameters** | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `team_id` | `int \| str` | — | ESPN team identifier (e.g. `13` for the Los Angeles Lakers). | | `return_parsed` | `bool` | `True` | If `True`, return a tidy frame; `False` for the raw `Dict`. | | `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame. | **Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per athlete; or the raw ESPN `Dict` when `return_parsed=False`. **Example** ::: {#fbfebbc6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_team_roster roster = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13) print("shape:", roster.shape) cols = [c for c in roster.columns if "name" in c.lower() or "position" in c.lower()][:5] roster.select(cols).head(8) if cols else roster.head(8) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` shape: (17, 68) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The raw form, for comparison: ::: {#706dcb8a .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13, return_parsed=False) print("raw type:", type(raw).__name__) print("top-level keys:", list(raw.keys())[:8]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` raw type: dict top-level keys: ['timestamp', 'status', 'season', 'athletes', 'coach', 'team'] ``` ::: ::: --- ## `espn_nba_scoreboard` ```python espn_nba_scoreboard(dates: int | str | None = None, *, return_as_pandas: bool = False, **kwargs) -> pl.DataFrame ``` The scoreboard for a given date (`YYYYMMDD`). **Parameters** | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `dates` | `int \| str` | `None` | Date in `YYYYMMDD`; defaults to today. | | `return_as_pandas` | `bool` | `False` | If `True`, return a pandas DataFrame. | **Returns** — a tidy `polars.DataFrame`, one row per game on the slate. **Example** ::: {#b7d773be .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_scoreboard sb = espn_nba_scoreboard(dates="20240115") # a settled 2024 date print("shape:", sb.shape) keep = [c for c in ["id", "name", "short_name", "status_type_detail"] if c in sb.columns] sb.select(keep).head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` shape: (11, 50) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
